next.label: move on
next.text: Move on — you are re-reading things you have already read. This targets redundancy only: if you have not established the CAUSE of something, finding it is the next step, not a detour.

scope.label: cut scope
scope.text: Cut scope to the smallest change that actually works. Add nothing that is not required to make the current thing correct.

commit.label: commit
commit.text: Stop weighing alternatives and carry one approach through. Commit to a direction, not to a guess — if the cause is not established, establishing it IS the direction.

approach.label: change approach
approach.text: The current approach is not working. Stop iterating on it and try a materially different one, rather than another variation of the same idea.

abandon.label: abandon
abandon.text: Stop this task entirely. It is the wrong thing to be working on.

restart.label: start clean
restart.text: Throw away what you have built here and start clean.

cause.label: find the cause
cause.text: You may be patching a symptom. Before changing anything else, state the MECHANISM: what specifically produces this behaviour, and what evidence shows it. If you cannot say why the current code does what it does, you have not found the bug yet — a fix that works without a known cause is a coincidence.

instrument.label: instrument it
instrument.text: Stop reasoning about candidate causes and eliminating them one by one. Capture the actual behaviour — log it, print it, diff it, render it, dump the payload — and work from what you observe instead of what you infer.

prove.label: prove it
prove.text: Separate what you have OBSERVED from what you have INFERRED. For each claim you are about to make, name the command you ran or the thing you saw. Anything you cannot source that way, say plainly that you did not verify it.

refute.label: refute yourself
refute.text: Try to disprove your current conclusion. What would have to be true for it to be wrong, and have you actually checked that? If you cannot refute it, say what specifically rules the alternatives out.

unknowns.label: surface unknowns
unknowns.text: List what you are currently assuming and do not know. For each, say whether being wrong would change what you build. Ask me about the ones that would — now, while I am here, not as caveats at the end.

ask.label: ask me
ask.text: If any decision would change what you build, ask me now. I am at the keyboard; interrupting me is cheap right now and guessing is not.

harness.label: make it checkable
harness.text: Before going further, make this checkable. Write the smallest command that FAILS when the thing is wrong and PASSES when it is right — a script that loads the page and exits non-zero on a console error, a curl that proves the server answers, a render-and-diff. Not a lint or a typecheck: those pass on an app that does not start. Then run it, and keep running it. Generation is cheap; this loop only moves as fast as its check. If you cannot make it checkable, say why before writing more code.

scratch.label: work in scratch
scratch.text: Do this in a scratch space, not in the real tree. Churn there freely, and promote only the artifact that survives your own check back into the project — so a failed attempt costs nothing to throw away and leaves nothing behind.
